title: Disclosure filing leads
summary: Counts from a city's export of agency reports: behested payment reports by the official named on them.

sections.heading: What it shows
paragraphs: Cities publish the reports their agencies and officials file on four state forms: payments to the agency (Form 801), ticket distributions (Form 802), behested payments (Form 803) and paid appointments (Form 806). The filing portal offers the list as a file to download. When that file is imported as a table, the app counts the reports of each form and, for behested payments, the reports naming each official.

A behested payment is a payment made to a third party, often a charity or a public event, at an official's request. The official files the report. The lead names an official only with three or more reports, and counts reports that name no official apart.

sections.heading: What it does not show
paragraphs: That a payment influenced a decision. The export gives a short description of each report and has no amount column; the payor, the payee and the amount are on the filed form.
How officials compare. A larger count can mean an office reports more completely, and the export covers only the dates chosen when it was downloaded.

sections.heading: Getting the file
paragraphs: On the City of San Diego's filing portal, search agency reports for a date range and use the export button to download the list as CSV, then import it under Analysis. The app does not download from this portal by itself.

sections.heading: How it is labelled
paragraphs: Basis: Pattern signal, not a legal claim. Confidence is not assessed: the finding restates counts of filed reports and infers nothing to score.
